steps.title: Prepare YP media
steps.instruction: Dissolve 20 g Bacto tryptone, 10 g yeast extract per litre of ddH₂O (up to 1 L). Autoclave the same day after preparation. Store at room temperature for long term.

steps.title: Prepare HR buffer
steps.instruction: Make 33 % v/w polyethylene glycol 50 % (autoclave), 100 mM lithium acetate 1 M (sterile‑filter), add salmon sperm DNA to 138.88 ng/µL (10 mg/mL stock) and DNA cassette to 2.7 ng/µL. Bring volume to 360 µL with ddH₂O. Store PEG solution at room temperature, LiAc at room temperature, DNA at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 2× SDS sample buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 100 mM Tris‑HCl pH 6.8, 4 % SDS, 20 % glycerol, 0.2 % bromophenol blue (10 mg), 100 mM DTT (4 M stock), and ddH₂O up to 50 mL. Store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare TBS buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 500 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 87.6 g sodium chloride (1.5 M) in water up to 1 L. Store at room temperature for up to 1 year.

steps.title: Prepare MP1 buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 100 mM Tris (1 M stock, 10 mL), 10 mM 1,4‑dithiothreitol (4 M stock, 0.25 mL) and ddH₂O to 100 mL. Use fresh.

steps.title: Prepare MP2 buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 1.2 M sorbitol (2.4 M stock, 125 mL), 120 mg Zymolyase (3 mg/g wet cells), 20 mM potassium phosphate (1 M pH 7.4, 5 mL) and ddH₂O to 250 mL. Use fresh.

steps.title: Prepare Homogenization buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.4 (1 M stock, 5 mL), 1 mM PMSF (200 mM stock, 1 mL), 1 mM EDTA (0.5 M pH 8 stock, 1 mL), 0.6 M sorbitol (2.4 M stock, 125 mL) and ddH₂O to 500 mL. Use fresh.

steps.title: Prepare SH buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 20 mM HEPES‑KOH pH 7.4 (1 M stock, 1 mL), 600 mM sorbitol (2.4 M stock, 12.5 mL) and ddH₂O to 50 mL. Use fresh.

steps.title: Prepare RIPA buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 1 % w/v Tergitol (NP‑40, 10 g), 1 mM EDTA (0.292 g), 1 mM EGTA (0.38 g), 0.1 % w/v SDS (0.380 g), 0.5 % w/v sodium deoxycholate (5 g) in water up to 1 L. Add one Roche protease‑cocktail tablet per 50 mL just before use. Store at 4 °C for up to 4 months.

steps.title: Prepare TAP buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 50 mM HEPES‑KOH pH 8.0, 100 mM KCl (2.98 g), 10 % v/v glycerol (1.86 g), 2 mM EDTA and ddH₂O to 250 mL. Store at 4 °C for up to 4 months.

steps.title: Prepare ABC buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate in water up to 50 mL. Make fresh and use within 24 h.

steps.title: Prepare StageTip conditioning buffer 2
steps.instruction: Mix 30 % v/v methanol (3 mL) with 0.2 % v/v trifluoroacetic acid (20 µL) and LC‑MS grade water to 6.98 mL. Prepare fresh; handle TFA with gloves in a fume hood.

steps.title: Prepare StageTip conditioning buffer 3 / wash buffer 2
steps.instruction: Mix 0.2 % v/v TFA (20 µL) with LC‑MS grade water to 9.98 mL. Prepare fresh; handle TFA with gloves.

steps.title: Prepare StageTip wash buffer 1
steps.instruction: Combine 1 % v/v TFA (0.1 µL) with 99 % v/v isopropanol (9.9 mL) and LC‑MS grade water to 10 mL. Prepare fresh; handle TFA with gloves.

steps.title: Prepare StageTip elution buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 80 % v/v acetonitrile (8 mL) with 1.25 % v/v NH₄OH (25 % stock, 0.5 mL) and LC‑MS grade water to 1.5 L. Prepare fresh immediately before use.

steps.title: Prepare MS loading buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 2 % v/v acetonitrile (0.2 mL) with 0.3 % v/v TFA (30 µL) and LC‑MS grade water to 10 mL. Prepare fresh; handle TFA with gloves.

steps.title: Thaw mitochondria
steps.instruction: Thaw 3 mg total mitochondrial protein per biological replicate on ice or at 4 °C.

steps.title: Solubilize mitochondria in SDS
steps.instruction: Spin mitochondria 10 min at 10,000 × g, 4 °C. Remove supernatant, add 300 µL 1 % SDS, incubate 5 min at 50 °C.

steps.title: Dilute lysate with RIPA and Benzonase
steps.instruction: Add 2,700 µL RIPA buffer containing 500 U Benzonase to the SDS lysate, incubate 30 min on ice (4 °C).

steps.title: Clarify lysate
steps.instruction: Spin at 16,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, transfer supernatant to a fresh 15 mL tube.

steps.title: Equilibrate streptavidin beads
steps.instruction: Resuspend streptavidin magnetic beads (60 µL bead slurry, 50 µg protein/µL) in 1 mL RIPA buffer, spin down, discard supernatant, add beads to the mitochondrial lysate tube.

steps.title: Bind biotinylated proteins
steps.instruction: Incubate the lysate‑bead mixture on a rotary shaker for 3 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Separate beads from lysate
steps.instruction: Pellet beads by centrifugation at 3,000 × g for 5 min at ~21 °C or by magnetic capture. Ensure all beads are at the bottom; avoid brown‑tinged supernatant.

steps.title: Wash beads
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL RIPA buffer, transfer beads to a fresh 1.5 mL tube on a magnetic rack, remove buffer. Repeat RIPA wash once more. Then wash twice with 1 mL TAP lysis buffer, followed by three washes with 1 mL freshly prepared ABC buffer.

steps.title: Digest proteins on‑bead (first round)
steps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 200 µL ABC buffer, add 1 µg sequencing‑grade modified trypsin, incubate 12–16 h at 37 °C with constant shaking.

steps.title: Digest proteins on‑bead (second round)
steps.instruction: Add an additional 1 µg trypsin to the bead suspension, incubate 3 h at 37 °C with constant shaking.

steps.title: Collect peptide eluates
steps.instruction: Harvest the clear supernatant (first eluate). Resuspend beads twice in 150 µL ABC buffer, collect each supernatant. Combine all three supernatants (total ≈ 500 µL).

steps.title: Finalize eluate and store
steps.instruction: Place tubes on magnetic rack for 5 min, transfer eluate to a new tube. Store at –80 °C if needed.

steps.title: Lyophilize peptide eluates
steps.instruction: Dry eluates in a SpeedVac vacuum concentrator until solvent is removed.

steps.title: Resuspend peptides for StageTip
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL 0.1 % TFA, incubate 10 min at 4 °C. Verify pH 2–3; adjust with 1 % TFA if necessary.

steps.title: Prepare StageTips
steps.instruction: Pack two layers of SDB‑RPS extraction disk into a 200 µL pipette tip using a 16‑gauge Kel‑F hub needle (part 90516) and a 1 mm OD metal wire to push the plugs down.

steps.title: Equilibrate StageTips
steps.instruction: Sequentially add 50 µL acetonitrile, 50 µL Conditioning Buffer 2, and 50 µL Conditioning Buffer 3 to each StageTip. Centrifuge 5–8 min at 1,500 × g, ~21 °C, until flow stops.

steps.title: Load samples onto StageTips
steps.instruction: Apply each peptide sample to its prepared StageTip.

steps.title: Wash StageTips
steps.instruction: Wash sequentially with Wash Buffer 1 then Wash Buffer 2; centrifuge 5–8 min at 1,500 × g, ~21 °C until flow stops.

steps.title: Elute peptides
steps.instruction: Elute with 60 µL elution buffer, collect into a low‑binding tube, centrifuge 5 min at 500 × g, ~21 °C until flow stops.

steps.title: Dry eluates
steps.instruction: Lyophilize in a vacuum concentrator for 30 min at 45 °C until ~2 µL remains.

steps.title: Resuspend for LC‑MS
steps.instruction: Add 15 µL MS loading buffer (2 % ACN, 0.3 % TFA), sonicate to dissolve. Store at –80 °C if not immediately analyzed.

steps.title: Inject samples into LC‑MS
steps.instruction: Place samples in the LC autosampler cooled to 4–8 °C. Inject 5 µL of each sample using the LC‑MS configuration described in Materials and Equipment.

steps.title: Process raw data with MaxQuant
steps.instruction: Run MaxQuant (e.g., v1.6.15.0) on the raw files using parameters from the provided mqpar.xml. Note that the authors used v1.5.2.8; later versions may give slightly different results.

steps.title: Install R and required packages
steps.instruction: Install RStudio v1.3.959+ and R v4.0.2+ on Windows. Required packages (installed automatically) are: dplyr≥0.8.3, stringr≥0.4.0, MASS≥7.3‑5.4, plotly≥4.9.0, htmlwidgets≥0.3, limma≥3.42.0, qvalue≥2.8.0.

steps.title: Download BioID analysis scripts
steps.instruction: Clone the GitHub repository https://github.com/wasimaftab/BioID_Proteomics. Place limma_main.R, limma_helper_functions.R and the MaxQuant output file proteingroups.txt (with iBAQ/LFQ values) in the same directory.

steps.title: Run limma analysis
steps.instruction: Open limma_main.R in RStudio and click Source. Select the proteingroups.txt file. The script will verify the presence of yeast mitochondrial proteins, remove non‑mitochondrial entries, log‑transform intensities, impute missing values, and apply an empirical Bayes moderated t‑test.

steps.title: Normalize and filter (optional)
steps.instruction: When prompted, choose whether to median‑normalize the data and/or remove exclusive proteins (those with zero intensity in all replicates of a group). The script will generate box‑plots and histograms for before/after normalization and imputation.

steps.title: Generate results
steps.instruction: After successful execution, a folder named “Results_<timestamp>” is created containing an HTML volcano plot, a TSV file with final statistics, and separate TSVs for any exclusively enriched proteins.

steps.title: Visualize and save volcano plot
steps.instruction: Open the HTML volcano plot in any web browser and save it as a PNG file if desired.

description: Here we describe a proximity labeling technique optimized for studying proteins in yeast mitochondria. Importantly, BioID (biotin identification) permits the identification of transiently interacting proteins and also proteins located in vicinity of the bait, which may not be co-purified by conventional pull down experiments (Roux et al., 2012; Sears et al., 2019). Generally, BioID is based on the biotinylation performed by a mutated form of a biotin ligase of bacterial origin, BirA. The modified version of BirA used in BioID (BirA∗) carries a mutation (R118G), which consents promiscuous biotinylation of the proteins included within the labeling radius, calculated to be about 10 nm (Choi-Rhee et al., 2004; Kim et al., 2014). There are four essential aspects of this optimized protocol. First, the targeted protein is only present as a BirA∗-fused variant expressed from the authentic promotor. This excludes non-assembled (and hence non-physiological forms of the proteins) that can disturb the analyses; this is in turn important to detect proximity interactions of proteins assembled into functional complexes. Second, to increase sensitivity and specificity, mitochondria are prepared prior to isolation of the biotinylated proteins. Third, proteins are purified under stringent denaturing conditions (which again decreases the likelihood to purify intact complexes), resulting in increased specificity. Fourth, subsequent mass spectrometric and bioinformatics analyses are streamlined for facile visualization and coherent statistical treatment.
